summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 (RHEL 7.9) with the specified ed25519 public key for SSH access and enforced key-based-only SSH authentication (PasswordAuthentication no, PubkeyAuthentication yes, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no). Verified end-to-end via live SSH: pubkey login succeeds, password/keyboard-interactive login is refused. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol on node1, proving boot_id changed and that sshd, the opsadmin account, its authorized_keys, and the key-only auth policy all survived the reboot intact.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline: RHEL 7.9, opsadmin user absent, no home dir
Created opsadmin user, home dir, .ssh (700), authorized_keys (600) with the required public key, correct ownership

Discovered sshd_config had conflicting PasswordAuthentication directives (line 65 'yes' appearing before line 141 'no'); since OpenSSH applies first-match-wins per keyword, effective policy was still password-enabled despite the trailing 'no' line
Backed up sshd_config, fixed line 65 to 'PasswordAuthentication no', validated with sshd -t, reloaded sshd
Verified effective config via sshd -T: pubkeyauthentication yes, passwordauthentication no, kbdinteractiveauthentication no

Functionally tested SSH: pubkey login succeeded with a temporary test key added to authorized_keys; a login attempt with PubkeyAuthentication disabled was rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey,...)'
Removed test key artifacts, restored authorized_keys to contain only the required key (verified 1 line, correct permissions)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, sshd active, opsadmin present, effective sshd config
Issued reboot via 'shutdown -r now' in background; connection drop served as the acknowledgment
Polled node1 until reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed (151c4aa9-9e81-4a32-9c22-08c5c441403a -> 1b3203e5-a54b-462c-a222-2fcbffec32c2) and uptime reset, proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart verified sshd active, opsadmin account intact, authorized_keys unchanged (exact required key, correct permissions), and effective sshd config still password-disabled/pubkey-enabled
Post-restart functional SSH retest: pubkey login succeeded, password/no-pubkey login attempt was refused
Cleaned up all test-key artifacts, leaving authorized_keys with exactly the one required key

evidence.requirement: opsadmin user created with required SSH public key installed
evidence.summary: Baseline showed opsadmin absent; user was created and authorized_keys populated with exactly the required ed25519 key, verified with correct ownership/permissions (600 file, 700 dir) and single-line content.

evidence.requirement: SSH configured to require key-based authentication (password auth disabled)
evidence.summary: Found a conflicting duplicate directive causing password auth to remain effectively enabled despite an existing trailing 'no' line (OpenSSH first-match-wins); fixed the first occurrence, validated with sshd -t, reloaded, and confirmed via sshd -T that passwordauthentication=[REDACTED] and pubkeyauthentication=yes cluster-wide.

evidence.requirement: Functional proof key-based login works and password login is rejected
evidence.summary: Live SSH session as opsadmin succeeded using a public-key credential; a login attempt with pubkey auth disabled was rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey,...)', confirming enforcement end-to-end pre-restart.
Captured boot_id (151c4aa9-9e81-4a32-9c22-08c5c441403a), uptime, sshd active status, opsadmin identity, and effective sshd auth config before reboot.

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgment and changed boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged via connection drop; node was unreachable during restart; reconnection showed a new boot_id (1b3203e5-a54b-462c-a222-2fcbffec32c2) and fresh uptime timestamp, proving an actual OS restart rather than a service bounce.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of services, account, and SSH policy on node1
evidence.summary: After restart, sshd was active, opsadmin still existed with its home/.ssh intact, authorized_keys retained the required key, and sshd -T still reported password auth disabled/pubkey enabled; a live SSH functional retest confirmed pubkey login success and password login refusal, then test artifacts were cleaned up leaving only the required key.
